legend: In contrast to pulmonary hamartoma, the pulmonary chondromas associated with Carney triad do not show entrapped respiratory epithelium between the lobules of cartilage and do not contain other mesenchymal elements such as fat, smooth muscle, or myxoid spindle cells.

legend: Immunohistochemistry for SDHB is not always easy to interpret. In this paraganglioma associated with germline mutation, there is a diffuse cytoplasmic blush in all the neoplastic cells. Because this staining contrasts with the intense granular expression in non-neoplastic internal controls, the tumour is still considered to be succinate dehydrogenase–deficient.

Immunohistochemistry for SDHB in a succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour. There is no expression of SDHB in any of the neoplastic cells. The granular cytoplasmic expression in the non-neoplastic cells, which acts as an internal positive control, is emphasized.

Morphological clues to succinate dehydrogenase–deficient paragangliomas are inconsistent but include well-developed, almost circular nests of epithelioid cells, sometimes with pale or vacuolated cytoplasm {31789631}.
Succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour commonly demonstrates a multilobulated or plexiform growth pattern.

Loss of expression of SDHB in succinate dehydrogenase–deficient paraganglioma. The presence of distinct granular staining in the non-neoplastic cells, which contrasts with the pale diffuse cytoplasmic blush in the neoplastic cells, is emphasized.
This phaeochromocytoma not associated with SDH mutation demonstrates diffuse strong SDHB expression. The cytoplasmic and distinctly granular (mitochondrial) pattern of expression is noted.
Succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour commonly demonstrates a multilobulated or plexiform growth pattern.
Succinate dehydrogenase–deficient gastrointestinal stromal tumour is usually epithelioid or epithelioid-predominant. Sometimes the epithelioid cells demonstrate a vaguely nested architecture.
This succinate dehydrogenase–deficient PitNET is indistinguishable morphologically from a sporadic tumour.
This example, associated with SDHA mutation, demonstrates loss of expression of both SDHB and SDHA by immunohistochemistry.
This example, associated with SDHA mutation, demonstrates loss of expression of both SDHB and SDHA (SDHA immunohistochemistry shown here).

legend: Immunohistochemistry for SDHB may be difficult to interpret. In this case, the weak cytoplasmic blush in the neoplastic cells contrasts markedly with the strong granular expression in the internal controls. This tumour should be considered succinate dehydrogenase–deficient.

The SDH complex comprises two anchoring subunits, SDHC and SDHD; the catalytic components SDHA and SDHB; and SDHAF2, responsible for the flavination of the SDHA component of the complex. If any component of the SDH complex is lost, the complex becomes dysfunctional and SDHB immunohistochemistry becomes negative. PPGL, paraganglioma and/or phaeochromocytoma.
